claims.text: In TLS the server authenticates with a certificate the client checks; client authentication is optional and happens only when the server sends a CertificateRequest during the handshake.
claims.source_hint: RFC 8446 §2 (server always authenticated, client optionally), §4.3.2 Certificate Request

claims.text: After a CertificateRequest the client sends its Certificate and a CertificateVerify, a signature over the handshake so far made with the private key matching that certificate; the server verifies it with the certificate's public key, which proves the client holds the key.
claims.source_hint: RFC 8446 §4.4.2 Certificate, §4.4.3 Certificate Verify

claims.text: A server requiring a client certificate aborts the handshake with an alert when none is sent (TLS 1.3: certificate_required) or when its chain does not reach a trusted CA (unknown_ca); it also rejects one no longer valid.
claims.source_hint: RFC 8446 §4.4.2.4 Receiving a Certificate Message, §6.2 Error Alerts (certificate_required, unknown_ca, certificate_expired)

claims.text: Mutual TLS uses the same record protection (encryption) as server-only TLS; what it adds is the client's Certificate and CertificateVerify in the handshake.
claims.source_hint: RFC 8446 §4.4 Authentication Messages, §5 Record Protocol

claims.text: Caddy is a web server configured by a Caddyfile. tls directive: client_auth { mode require_and_verify } requires a client certificate and verifies it; trust_pool file <pem> loads the CA certificates trusted to sign client certificates.
claims.source_hint: Caddy 2.10 docs: Caddyfile directives > tls > client_auth (mode, trust_pool file)

claims.text: Caddy placeholder {http.request.tls.client.subject} is the subject of the client certificate; respond answers every request with the given body (output: hello CN=gateway-client).
claims.source_hint: Caddy 2.10 docs: Caddyfile concepts > placeholders (http.request.tls.client.*); directives > respond

claims.text: With require_and_verify and only a trust_pool, Caddy accepts any client certificate that chains to a CA in the pool; it does not restrict which subject names may connect.
claims.source_hint: Caddy 2.10 docs: tls > client_auth (verifier/leaf options are separate, unused here); echo-mtls.yaml lines 17-22

claims.text: A cert-manager CA Issuer writes tls.crt, tls.key and ca.crt into each Certificate's Secret and renews it before expiry. Getting the CA to every peer is separate; cert-manager's docs advise against mounting ca.crt as a real trust pool, as the lab does, since it changes on renewal.
claims.source_hint: cert-manager 1.20 docs: Configuration > CA issuer; Usage > Certificate resources (renewal); k8s.l3.cert-manager summary 3-4

claims.text: Certificate spec.usages 'server auth' / 'client auth' set the certificate's extended key usage, printed by openssl as TLS Web Server / Client Authentication; spec.commonName sets the CN in the subject, the certificate's name.
claims.source_hint: cert-manager 1.20 docs: Usage > Certificate resources (usages, commonName); mutual-tls.txt lines 12-22
